description: What low food does to a player on RotN 3.3.4: Hunger Overhaul's low-food potion effects (by food level and difficulty), starvation, the constant hunger drain and the regeneration floor. Hand-written from the bytecode of Hunger Overhaul 1.3.3 (jenkins 148), AppleCore 3.4.0 and the vanilla 1.12.2 server jar of the pinned pack zip, read with javap only, and from the pack's configs; excerpts and copies in packages/rotn-data/test/fixtures/hunger-effects-3.3.4/. confidence 'verified' = read from that bytecode and config; nothing here was watched in a run.
summary: On the test server (difficulty 2, Normal), from food 4 down Hunger Overhaul keeps Mining Fatigue and Slowness on the player, from I at food 4 to IV at food 1 or 0. Weakness comes at food 2 (I) and 1 (II), Nausea at food 1. Mining Fatigue multiplies dig speed by 0.3, 0.09, 0.0027 and 0.00081 (I to IV), so from food 3 any dig harder than a crop is about 11 times slower and from food 2 it is effectively impossible (dirt by hand: 750 ms, 2.5 s at I, 8.3 s at II, 278 s at III, 926 s at IV). Each effect lasts 19 ticks and is renewed every 10 ticks while food stays low; the server removes it when food rises (or the player dies). Food 0 for 80 ticks kills: 200 starvation damage at any difficulty and health. At rest Hunger Overhaul's constant drain takes 1 point (saturation first, then food) about every 235 s (about 15 per hour); activity adds vanilla's exhaustion on top. No health regeneration below food 7.

config.note: the active config; default.cfg and blankslate.cfg in the same folder are presets

sources.difficulty: server.properties line 12 difficulty=2 (Normal); deploy/test-server/build.sh configure_server never changes it; config/Universal Tweaks - Tweaks.cfg line 555 and config/defaultoptions.cfg line 10 default new worlds to NORMAL (not locked). Not read from a running server.

effects.rule: HungerOverhaulEventHook.onLivingUpdate, every 10 ticks (an NBT countdown 'HungerOverhaulCheck' set to 9) for a player that is alive and not in creative: d = the world difficulty id (Peaceful 0 .. Hard 3) when difficultyScalingEffects is true, else 2. For each effect the first tier whose food bound holds is checked; it applies only if d >= minDifficulty, and then no later tier is tried. The effect is PotionEffect(effect, 19 ticks, amplifier, ambient true, particles true). Amplifier 0 = level I.

byFoodAtServerDifficulty.note: The tiers above at d = 2 (the test server). Amplifier per effect; absent = no effect. Food 5 and above: none.

miningFatigueDigFactor.note: Vanilla EntityPlayer.getDigSpeed: the dig speed is multiplied by this per Mining Fatigue amplifier (3 and above: 0.00081).

effects.afterDeath: The server's new player entity has no effects and sends no remove_entity_effect; a client that keeps the old entity (mineflayer) must drop its own copy on respawn.

starvation.rule: AppleCore Hooks.onAppleCoreFoodStatsUpdate: while food is 0 or less the starve timer counts up each tick; at GetStarveTickPeriod (80 ticks) it fires StarvationEvent.Starve and calls attackEntityFrom(DamageSource.STARVE, starveDamage), then restarts the timer; food above 0 resets it. Starve's constructor sets 1, or 0 at health 10 or less on Easy or 1 or less on Normal (vanilla's rule); Hunger Overhaul's onStarve then sets damageOnStarve (200) unconditionally.

drain.rule: Hunger Overhaul adds 0.01 exhaustion every 10 ticks, 0.001 per tick (constantHungerLoss), on top of vanilla's sources; one point of saturation, or of food once saturation is 0, costs maxExhaustion = 4.0 / (hungerLossRatePercentage / 100), times 1.6667 on Peaceful and 1.3333 on Easy (difficultyScalingHunger).

regeneration.rule: FoodEventHandler.allowHealthRegen: natural regeneration only while food >= minHungerToHeal (7), healthRegenRatePercentage > 0, the naturalRegeneration game rule is on and the player is hurt; disableHealingHungerDrain means healing costs no food.

unverified: The test server's difficulty was not read from a running server (no log line prints it); it is the pack's server.properties value, which the harness never changes.
Nothing was watched in a run; soak 14's dig hangs (net-forge, /home/rv/soak14-net-forge.md) fit the table.
